l4.alert_evidence: Attributed via the AWS/Events rule metrics of defense-in-depth-agent-ip-injection-attempts on the central bus, which is the rule that fans both PromptInjectionAttempt and PromptLeakageDetected out to the alert topic. Before the topic-policy fix: TriggeredRules 4, Invocations 4, FailedInvocations 4 (every publish denied). After: TriggeredRules 2, Invocations 2, FailedInvocations 0. The topic-level NumberOfMessagesPublished metric lags by several minutes and is not per-event, so it is not used to decide this field.
l4.root_cause_fixed: The central alert topic's policy allowed events.amazonaws.com to publish only when aws:SourceAccount was a client account (Sid AllowEventBridgeFromClientAccount). The rules that fan out from the central bus run in the central account, so their SourceAccount is the central account and every publish was denied. Fixed by adding the central account to the condition; the before/after rule metrics above are the evidence that this was the cause.

l4.reason: Not triggerable on this model. Canary detection fires only when a canary token embedded in the base prompt appears in the model's raw output. Nova Lite recorded ASR 0/42 in every configuration except the C0 baseline, and zero CANARY LEAK DETECTED lines were emitted across all 1170 campaign requests, so the detector never had a leak to act on. The metric filter, alarm and forwarding path are deployed and identical in shape to the two rows verified above; what is unverified is the end-to-end firing, not the wiring.

l4.expected: CloudTrail rule forwards straight to the central alert topic
l4.note: monitoring.tf targets the central SNS topic directly, not the event bus, so bus_event_received is false by design for this row.
l4.alert_evidence: Per-rule metrics of defense-in-depth-agent-ip-lambda-modified (client account) from the trigger timestamp: TriggeredRules 1, FailedInvocations 0 at +52s; AWS/SNS NumberOfMessagesPublished on the central alert topic went 0 -> 1 at +53s. No other trigger was active in the window, so the publish is attributable to this event.
root_causes_fixed: Event pattern matched eventName exactly against 'UpdateFunctionConfiguration', but CloudTrail records the Lambda API with a version suffix (UpdateFunctionConfiguration20150331v2). Verified on 78 raw trail objects: 9 such events, none under the bare name. Rule never fired in any deployed version. Fixed with prefix matchers; Lambda is the only source in monitoring.tf that versions its event names.

After the pattern fix the rule fired but the publish failed. The SNS targets carry role_arn, so EventBridge publishes as the client role, not as the events.amazonaws.com service principal; the central topic policy had no statement for a client-account principal. Fixed by allowing sns:Publish to each client account root (the client's IAM scopes it to the eventbridge-sns role). This affected all six control-plane rules.
